newsitem.title: USA: U.S. wheat group urges MFN extension for China.
newsitem.headline: U.S. wheat group urges MFN extension for China.

text.p: National Association of Wheat Growers said Monday it supported renewal of most-favored-nation trade status for China for another year.
President Clinton must decide the issue by June 3.

"Failure to renew China's MFN status would put an end to our commercial agricultural relations, bringing an enormous negative impact to U.S. wheat farmers and the U.S. economy," the group said in a letter to Clinton.
Chinese purchases of U.S. wheat averaged 3.3 million tonnes annually over the past five years. But China has bought only 288,100 tonnes in 1996/97 marketing year ending May 31.

Sales have been disrupted by disagreement over TCK smut, a wheat fungus. China has refused to buy U.S. wheat without assurance the grain is free of the fungus. U.S. officials say the fungus poses on threat to China's agriculture sector.
